# Mathematics build operations

The deterministic `tools/autopilot/` engine owns dispatches and transitions. The
approved build checklist is [research/workflow-rebuild-plan.md](research/workflow-rebuild-plan.md); consult it when changing
this workflow. Mathematics and its sibling engine have separate revisions,
worker prompts, supporting tools, content and run state.

## Six-step workflow

| Step | Work | Agents and handoff |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Prerequisite drift, scaffolding and complete initial authoring | Existing drift agents and GPT-6 Luna/max authors; authored items, A/B pages, contracts, source evidence and manifests |
| 2 | Review, one local repair and owner escalation | Luna-max reviewers/local repairers; at most two reviews and one repair; owner/orchestrator resolves escalations and runs gates |
| 3 | Independent review | GPT-6 Luna/max readers and refuters; GPT-6.1 Sol/medium batch adjudicators; final validation and mechanical closure |
| 4 | Batch review and judging | GPT-6.1 Sol/medium read-only batch readers plus GPT-6 Luna/max judges |
| 5 | Adjudication and repair | Existing native repair, consumer maintenance, certification and gate routes |
| 6 | Closeout | Contracts, pathways, stamps, readiness, evidence, owner report and local closeout commit |

The former Step 2 assignment stage and former Step 4 splice/integration stage
are deleted. Necessary group metadata is generated mechanically during planning.
Accepted manifests are transcribed into the canonical plan at Step 2's existing
mechanical join, followed by the post-authoring snapshot. Neither operation has
its own agent or workflow stage. The pre-authoring snapshot runs before Step 1
construction. Initial item and page authoring happens entirely in Step 1;
later stages retain their substantive review, repair and finalization duties.

The Step-1 `content-policy-scaffold` gate retains its gate identity and joins
all current run manifests in authored-carrier mode, without `--manifest-only`.
It checks the completed items' provenance, source references and generated-claim
containment, together with manifest capacity and duplicate-ID checks. The
separate `manifest-deps` gate still requires explicit manifest dependency arrays.
Future-mint checks belong before authoring; existing Step-1 carriers do not need
the later canonical-plan transcription to qualify for authored-item validation.
Subsequent `content-policy-items` gates recheck the current authored carriers.

## Construction and escalation

Step 1 keeps existing drift/source recovery, readiness, scope, page-capacity and
owner-hold mechanisms. Initial authors use `gpt-6-luna-max`; drift/source recovery
retains its existing model assignments. Both drift reviewers and authors
must escalate significant unmet prerequisites directly to the owner, giving the
smallest missing supplier, consuming claims/steps and affected consumers.
Scaffolding agents fully author all assigned items, pages and proof contracts;
a proof strategy or successful process alone is not a completed carrier.
Readiness records bind the finished carriers. Cross-pair supplier completion
does not hold initial author dispatch; nonempty authored inventories and current
readiness remain required for acceptance.

After a confirmed planning defect is repaired, the owner may resolve its exact
`drift-blocked` verdict through `research/RUN-owner-drift-resolutions.json`
(version 1, `owner-resolved-drift-blockers`, `authorized_by: owner`). The receipt
binds the unchanged native report and full archived original report, successful
original native attempt/result and prompt, original drift evidence, and current
page scope/interfaces. Each resolution names the exact page/verdict, complete
archived source preimages and changed current raw source hashes, and focused
owner acceptance evidence referencing the genuine delegated repair evidence.
Consumer dispositions cover the companion and every direct/indirect planned
consumer. Missing, stale or ambiguous bindings fail closed; acceptance satisfies
only the named planning blocker. It grants no new worker execution, proof or
review coverage, rewrites no native evidence, and leaves all scope checks,
later reviews, recertification and complete gate batteries mandatory. The schema
and scope-digest calculation are in [tools/drift-owner-resolutions.md](tools/drift-owner-resolutions.md).

Construction readiness retains its snapshot and receipt-stamped decisions across
fresh controller contexts belonging to the same configuration and frontier.
Manifest, coverage, plan, consumed supplier and missing-dependency file stamps
guard reuse. When alias lookup is used, the entire item inventory is also
stamp-bound: any change rebuilds alias resolution together with dependency bytes
and readiness decisions. Failed input scans discard partial cached inputs and
keep the scaffold incomplete. Scheduling caches never certify changed inputs.

Planning and the existing drift-apply join write `research/RUN-batch-dependency-levels.json` before construction. Before each Step 1 dispatch the engine recomputes this artifact from current page requirements and manifest/carrier logical dependencies, rejects batch cycles, and includes the batch level and suppliers in the worker task. Batch level is zero without in-run suppliers, otherwise one plus their maximum level. Initial mathematics authoring uses `unitPrerequisitePolicy: 'priority'`: sort all pending pairs by dependency level before selecting slots, without waiting for cross-pair suppliers to finish. Fill the configured stage, role and global capacity, then refill immediately on worker completion; retain adoption and exclusive-writer guards. For 7, 6, 8 and 12 pairs in successive levels with 30 slots, start all 21 pairs in the first three levels and 9 in the fourth, then admit the next fourth-level pair whenever a slot opens. Authors continue independent work against declared interfaces and record unresolved supplier checks honestly; they cannot claim readiness or quote absent supplier bodies. Actual authored-carrier/readiness requirements, full gates, review and supplier-before-consumer repair remain mandatory. Other stages retain the default completion policy. External suppliers remain context.

Each dispatch pass shares a fresh manifest/alias snapshot across its dependency graph. Priority authors with disjoint outputs receive one fan-out graph check rather than one full graph rebuild per slot. Snapshots are confined to the current pass; subsequent dispatches read current inputs again.

Initial priority-author scheduling parses complete actual source `deps` fields
and any needed alias fields with the renderer's YAML parser, together with all
current manifests. Unrelated metadata being written by another author does not
block slot refill. A missing or unformed source frontmatter envelope is unfinished
construction input: its declared manifest/page dependencies remain, and available
source dependencies are read again on the next dispatch pass. This does not
certify that source or grant readiness. Complete present dependency/alias fields
that are malformed or duplicate, invalid manifests, ambiguous ownership and
cycles still fail closed; no batch or declared dependency is dropped. This narrow graph
projection records scheduling metadata only. Post-drain level recomputation,
ordinary level commands, readiness, reviews and every gate retain strict whole
frontmatter parsing and check the actual current carriers.

Item inventories and logical dependencies are determined in scaffold manifests before item carriers are written; authors compute labels there and construct carriers in ascending item level. Item `dependency_level` is recorded and independently checked in Step 1: zero
without in-run logical suppliers, otherwise one plus the maximum supplier level.
External suppliers remain context. No rebatching or additional review stage is introduced. Logical dependencies must agree between authored bodies and
manifests; aliases resolve to canonical suppliers. Definition discharges and
nonlogical links are hash-bound context, not extra logical scheduling edges.

## Whole-batch scope/prerequisite loop

Step 2 workers perform only substantive scope/prerequisite review, local source
repair and escalation. Each batch has a read-only `scope-reviewer` and a local
`scope-repairer`, both `gpt-6-luna-max`; reuse their respective sessions where
available. Each review covers the entire current batch, including additions and
complete A/B pages, before returning one consolidated result.

The sequence is review/accept -> ONE local repair -> final review/accept ->
escalate to the OWNER. The engine permits at most two complete reviews and one
local repair. Escalate immediately when a significant prerequisite gap cannot be
rigorously resolved locally on the same page. Other page-local defects receive
the single repair and final review. If the second review remains unsatisfied for
any reason, escalate; there is no second local repair or third engine review.
Failed processes and retries do not reset successful review/repair counters.

There is no prerequisite-completion dispatch barrier in Step 2. Share up to
30 active engine workers only among reviews and local repairs, and refill each
available slot immediately. There is no automatic owner-repair dispatch.
Independent assigned source scopes run concurrently; only overlapping authorized
write files wait for an active writer. Read-only consumer context does not reserve
worker slots or block another pair. Repairers write
directly to their assigned source files, without private workspaces. Inspect
actual suppliers before their consumers within each repair. Imported sources
remain read-only. Preserve approved claims, inventory promises and pair/page
identities; prove necessary intermediate results rather than dropping scope.

Whenever an original Statement/Definition changes, the same agent traces and
checks all direct and indirect consumers using old/current dependencies, aliases
and nonlogical uses. Physical public-interface changes have the same duty in
physics. Check actual supplier uses and assumptions; repair consumers within the
assigned source scope and report required outside repairs to the owner. Every
affected consumer appears in the substantive result, and the final reviewer
checks the local repair's consumer dispositions.

Workers have no hashing, rehashing, certification, recertification, numeric-level
reconciliation, manifest/coverage/proof-contract maintenance, evidence-ledger or
automated formatting/validator duties in Step 2. Their lightweight result contains
only identity, prepared inventory, round, decision, defect types, concise findings
and required consumer dispositions. The optional legacy hash report field serves
only already-running old workers; new workers do not compute or report hashes.
Honest uncertainty, rigorous complete arguments and faithful source use remain
substantive obligations. Existing manifests are navigation context, not worker
maintenance assignments.

The engine retains simple dispatch, routing, overlap coordination and the bounded
two-review/one-repair counters. Minimal pass receipts record dispositions and
counts. After the engine pass and worker drain, pause for the owner before the
Step-2 battery. Escalated pairs remain explicit holds. The owner/orchestrator
alone resolves escalations, handles metadata and recertification, and runs the
Step-2 gates. Preserve CLAUDE.md's maximum of two outside escalation-resolution
cycles; they are not additional engine review/local-repair rounds. Resolved owner
escalations receive direct acceptance without an engine re-review or counter reset.
The owner controls the battery and advancement to Step 3.

A Step-2 native worker that finishes after the tick's `onProgress` collection
boundary receives one same-tick grace from synthetic artifact-stalemate detection.
The next tick collects its genuine result and still detects any persistent
missing acceptance derivative. This grace is bounded to an in-memory set of
units active at that boundary; it records no coverage, changes no counters or
receipts, and does not affect acceptance, gates, existing holds or other stages.

The engine writes `research/RUN-step2-owner-pass.json` before the owner pause.
If remaining local work resumes, it drains and produces
`RUN-step2-owner-battery-ready.json`, pausing again before the battery. Neither
handoff performs recertification or grants gate authorization. The owner may
record resolved escalation acceptance from the content workspace:

```bash
node tools/batch-scope-review.mjs owner-resolve --run RUN --batch N --decision accept --reviewer OWNER --reason 'Exact resolution'
```

Historical `--decision continue` commands also accept directly. Apply owner
resolution only after source writers drain. This never dispatches another engine
review, restores a spent local repair, or replaces the orchestrator's pre-battery
work.

Finite-smoke obligations use named deterministic computations in `tools/finite-smoke.mjs` and exact source assertion excerpts in proof contracts. The registry includes finite covariance/rank, scalar Lasso and collinear-design witnesses, robust-estimator partition/rank/zero-data boundaries, deterministic replacement counterexamples, log-space binomial witnesses, bounded log-series checks for numerical constants, exact Rademacher and four-row regression witnesses, and finite Poisson-window and Strauss likelihood comparisons. Parameter values describe the finite model and must satisfy the check's domain. A finite-smoke pass checks only that model, not the general proof; a counterexample obligation passes when its stated false-claim witness is verified. Unknown names and stale assertion excerpts fail explicitly. Registry changes are validated by the authorized full gate battery; do not substitute an empty selection or fabricate success for an unsupported name.

Four finite Gaussian checks cover normal-normal posterior moments, working-normal coverage calibration, a truncated-normal support/TV witness, and one Gaussian-sequence coordinate's posterior and predictive law. `normal-normal-finite-n-posterior` uses n=1,2,5, tau=1/2,1,2 and sample means -2,0,3; `normal-working-model-calibration-boundary` uses z=1,2 and sigma=1/2,1,2, with alpha defined by the quantile relation; `boundary-posterior-support-and-tv-witness` uses n=1,4,16 and Delta=-2,0,2; `gaussian-sequence-one-coordinate-posterior` uses n=i=alpha=kappa_i=1 and observations -2,0,3. These fixed models use independent numerical integration of original Gaussian density products or interval probabilities, 4,096-panel Simpson quadrature, ten-standard-deviation moment windows and tolerance 1e-8. They do not verify CLTs, asymptotic posterior convergence, infinite products, or square-summable support. Their contract assertions must be exact source excerpts; fixture lists are fixed by the registry rather than contract parameters.

The `anisotropic-real-norm-complex-homogeneity-witness` check uses exact Gaussian-integer pairs `[real, imaginary]`, positive integer weights `[1,2]`, vector `[1,0]` and scalar `[0,1]` to recompute `N(1)=1`, `N(i)=2` and `|i|=1`. It rejects a witness satisfying complex homogeneity, a different source normalization, or incorrect claimed values. This is finite counterexample sanity evidence; it does not verify the real norm axioms for all real coordinates.

The `cyclotomic-rank-one-f5-inverse` check exhausts all 16 unit parameter pairs in F5 and independently searches all 25 quadratic residues for the inverse of X. The `cyclotomic-rank-one-content-collision` check reduces the actual rational specialization Q=2, u1=u2=1 using exact monic integer polynomial division, then checks every unit repeated root in F5. It verifies a nonzero square-zero element and vanishing interpolation denominator. These are bounded sanity checks for rank-one examples, not proofs for arbitrary fields or ranks.

During content-policy inventory reads, a missing carrier is retried five times
over at most 770 ms to tolerate concurrent replacement by another workflow.
Persistent absence and all other read errors still fail; no inventory entry,
scoped item, prerequisite, or policy check is omitted.

## Independent review through closeout

For an owner-authorized recovery of exactly two local, unpushed legacy whole-tree
closeout commits, `autopilot reopen-closeout --run RUN --state-dir .autopilot/RUN
--authorization research/RUN-closeout-reopen-authorization.json --inspect` reads
the exact guards without changing Git or state. The same command without
`--inspect` requires the sealed guards and a current owner scope policy, archives
the genuine native suffix history and original commits in a hash-bound bundle,
and compare-and-swaps only `main` to their parent. It preserves the current index
byte for byte and checks working file bytes/modes before and after the ref change.
Original pre-legacy outside staging remains explicitly unknown; it is never
reconstructed from the parent tree. Only `6-readiness-v2` through `6-close-v2`
reopens, paused; native restart/resume must rerun its actual gates, reporting and
scoped commit. Earlier stages and mathematical carriers remain untouched.

Step 3 uses independent batch review and routed adjudication after authoring in
dependency-level order. Step 3b is retired in both engines: there is no separate
cross-batch edge review, impact-review window or unfinished cross-review lane.
Step-3 readers and refuters use GPT-6 Luna/max; batch adjudicators use GPT-6.1
Sol/medium. Step-4 read-only batch readers use GPT-6.1 Sol/medium, and the
per-item judge sweep uses GPT-6 Luna/max.
The final sequence is `3a-baseline` then `3a-close`. The existing Step 3a
validation battery remains in adjudication. Mechanical closure checks exact
current item, contract, manifest and page carriers against the post-gate
snapshots and plan correspondence; it freezes evidence without repeating the
passed review or introducing another gate battery. Source and
empirical qualifications survive regeneration.

New closure receipts use version 3 with basis `dependency-ordered-step3a` and
bind the exact Step 3a evidence. Historical version-2 receipts remain verifiable
against their original evidence, including completed Step 3b work. Retiring the
stage grants no new review coverage, clears no confirmed defect and leaves
published-repair handoffs for their later independent judgments. Cross-batch
consumer defects found during review go to the owner for supplier-first repair;
they are not deferred to a retired stage.

An existing successful Step-3a `accepted_repair` verdict may retain its native
meaning after accompanying metadata reconciliation through explicit
`source_identical_acceptance_continuities` entries in the run's owner repair
evidence. Each guard binds the genuine native completion, assignment, report,
archived accepted decision and immutable reader-post carrier, requires exact
current source claim/dependency mirrors and an actual strict contract pass,
and preserves missing historical manifest projections as explicitly unknown.
This records acceptance continuity, never new worker coverage; it neither
stamps decisions nor waives any other gate.

The ordinary continuity case requires identical raw source bytes. A separately
hash-proven complete reader-post source preimage may also establish metadata
continuity when the entire current body is exactly identical and parsed
frontmatter differs only in `dependency_level`, `verification` or
`provenance`. Status, run, dependencies, sources, assumptions, proof strategy
and all other fields remain unchanged. Owner/delegated audit, source-audit and
published-repair markers may not be added or changed through this exception.
An unknown source delta is never classified as metadata from hashes alone.
A definition, algorithm or remark with no numbered proof may retain the exact
original/current null contract; proof-bearing missing contracts remain errors.

For a validated same-ID prerequisite rehome, native assignment and reader-post
snapshot bindings retain their original batch. Only current manifest and
contract lookups use the authenticated current home. Mechanical source-level
or verification changes require the complete archived before source to match
the immutable post-reader raw hash and the actual current mathematical source
to match the authenticated before/after rehome archives. Invalid receipts,
changed proof bodies and unsupported current contract inputs fail closed.

An owner may preserve a genuine native reader finding about an outside published
page through `RUN-step3-owner-required-page-routes.json` (version 1,
`owner-step3-required-published-page-route-v1`). This narrow routing receipt
binds the original unchanged finding, report, successful native attempt and
structured completion, prompt, immutable pre/post snapshots, current assigned
page manifest and its explicit `requires` edge. The assigned consumer must
reach an actual published item listed on that page through hash-bound current
logical dependency edges. The page must remain outside all run manifests.
Owner-current before and after archives, identical frontmatter, at most two
unique literal prose edits, and focused owner review bind the exact correction.
These archives establish no historical full-byte reader observation. The native
subject label and reader obligation remain unchanged; an explicit page carrier
route uses the actual published page bytes and never a fabricated item carrier.
The route grants no scope, edit authority, acceptance or review coverage. Normal
independent adjudication, explicit historical uncertainty, current page sealing,
defect-ledger closure and every gate remain mandatory. Unregistered foreign
findings retain the ordinary rejection; this receipt does not enlarge refuter
or owned-page inventories. The Step-3 closure freezes this exact optional registry
and its hash-bound native and owner historical evidence; later verification rejects
registry or referenced-evidence mutation.
A later native Step-5 manifest mirror repair may retain the route's exact old
manifest through its existing content-addressed supporting-metadata archive.
Closure accepts only the original expected hash, authenticated by a verified
current certificate, its identical frozen certificate, and a certificate-bound
native owner collection with its unchanged pack, reports and successful results.
The original closure still records the original manifest path/hash. Current
origin-page ownership, its explicit required-page edge, the same assigned
consumer and the published page's exclusion from run ownership are checked
separately. Other historical references remain strict; no registry or closure
is refreshed and no new historical observation or acceptance is supplied.
Downstream routes use that same archive authentication for their supplier and
consumer manifests, retaining exact historical and current subject inventories
and current unique draft ownership and direct dependency checks. An authentic
owner-captured original preimage absent from Step-5 certification may instead be
bound by `RUN-step3-owner-manifest-continuities.json` (version 1,
`owner-step3-historical-manifest-continuity`). This explicit root historical-only
receipt binds the unchanged original registry, exact route/index/reference,
original closed Step-3 receipt and successful native close result, recovered raw
preimage and earlier owner receipt pinning its original hash. Durable copies of
both original owner evidence files must live in run-owned `research/`; original
runtime paths may remain provenance metadata but are not future inputs. Creation
requires an archived paused/drained 5.9 state with the exact native ledger failure
naming that changed downstream manifest. The original closure path/hash remains;
no prior certificate binding, native observation or mathematical acceptance is
invented. Missing or changed evidence fails closed; other historical references
stay strict and all gates retain their ordinary current inputs.

When a reader repairs some defects but cannot resolve another in the same
draft, the owner may retain its original open finding through
`RUN-step3-owner-partial-reader-repairs.json`. This routing-only record binds
the genuine successful reader result, unchanged report, frozen post-reader
snapshot and exact remaining findings/carriers. Both touched and reader
obligations remain; normal independent adjudication, ledger closure and all
gates are still required. Missing or changed authority fails closed.

A definition may acquire its first real proof contract after its frozen
pre-reader snapshot; routing preserves the original null contract hash and
requires the current contract. A reader's intermediate supplier observation
whose source bytes were not retained may be registered in
`RUN-step3-owner-unbound-reader-observations.json`, bound to the exact successful
reader receipt and unchanged finding/report. The original reported digest stays
visible, but the observation is explicitly unbound: historical uncertainty,
independent current-source review, ledger closure and all gates remain required.

The existing one-shot native refuter coverage continuation also handles a
completed report that omits an assigned subject. Archive the exact original
report/result, drain writers and bind the complete current refuter inventory
before dispatch. A truncated native diagnostic tail must match a substantial exact
raw archived-report suffix containing the not-opened and flagged fields; the
unchanged hash-bound full report supplies the original observations. Only a fresh
successful native correction result supplies coverage; never add an unread subject to the old report or waive collection.

Outside published-supplier alerts in native Step-4 digests retain their exact
original bytes. The owner may record `research/RUN-step4-published-alert-routes.json`
(version 1, `owner-routed-step4-published-alerts`, `authorized_by: owner`). Each
route binds the unchanged digest, exact alert index and object, successful native
reader attempt and original structured output, focused owner evidence, and the
current policy-valid recorded published repair. Digests and later alert routing
validate that receipt; published routes remain separately visible in the derived
alert inventory and never acquire a fabricated in-run owner or new review coverage.
Original Step-3 closure and judge verdicts remain immutable. Existing judge
currency rules continue to govern unchanged consumer carriers.

Step-4 alerts about another batch's in-run page route to its actual page-owning
group, just as item alerts route to their item-owning group. Same-batch findings
belong in concerns. Page findings retain ordinary owning-group disposition and
page currency guards; they cannot license an item repair or supply judge coverage.

Step 4's read-only
batch digests use `RUN-batch-N-step5-context.json`; a digest from another batch
cannot cover the inventory, and retries target only failing batches.

Step 5 retains the round-based adjudication/repair engine, supplier-before-consumer
maintenance, frozen frontier guards and its complete gate battery. The
judgment/adjudication rounds continue until the latest round has zero items
deemed defective by adjudicators (zero unique confirmed-fatal items across all
adjudicated subjects). Any confirmed-fatal item requires another round, even if
repaired within that round; uncertainty, missing adjudications and unresolved
defects still block closure. The frozen original inventory remains unchanged.
Step 5 rejudgment uses GPT-6.1 Sol at high reasoning effort, independent of the
Step-4 judge model.
Step-5 final judge closure retains the genuine frozen Step-4 Luna verdicts for
original-frontier items whose guard text is unchanged from the native baseline.
Changed items require current Sol evidence, subject to the existing current
central-certification policy. A selective closure joins the complete immutable
frontier, hash-bound baseline and original native verdict inventory; it never
accepts arbitrary models, invents verdicts or drops subjects. All normal item/context
currency and exact rejection-adjudication checks continue to apply.
Genuine native Step-5 helper creations stay separate from that frozen original
frontier. Selective closure requires exactly all original IDs plus all creations
from the authenticated native certificate, with no unknown, duplicate or omitted
subject. Original baseline/Luna checks remain unchanged; helpers acquire no
invented original verdict and require the existing current central certification
or genuine current Sol evidence under ordinary closure currency checks.
Repeated adjudication consumes the actual rejudge verdicts.
An explicit native confirmed-fatal supplier scope blocker may receive a separately
attributed current root repair review through the guarded
[version-2 owner supplement](tools/step5-owner-scope-blocker.md). The unchanged
native finding, successful dispatch and paused/drained creation state remain
bound; genuine supplier and blocker repairs, complete affected-consumer inventory,
current reviews and source reading are mandatory. Original fatal counts and all
later gates remain; this supplies no new native execution or judge credit.
The same guarded loader has a separate version-3 form for a completed native
assigned repair that explicitly routes a fatal open direct result supplier. It
binds the original paused/drained pre-gate state, exact native finding and
supplier preimage, genuine Statement repair, recursively complete affected
consumer inventory and current root reviews. It requires no artificial gate
failure and preserves the native decision, observations and fatal counts.
Terminal judge stamps and mechanical coverage use the same per-item policy and
stamp the actual judging model. When an item has no verification mapping or
source block, its first judge-only verification mapping is inserted immediately
after the opening frontmatter delimiter. Removing that mapping must recover the
original guard and judge representations exactly; stamping cannot change item
currency through separator whitespace. A guarded native `record-operational-supplement`
may reconcile a coverage-only diagnostic from an incorrect lineup descriptor.
Creation requires the exact paused native repair stage and drained successful
workers; it binds their unchanged reports, assignment, diagnostics, original
frontier/baseline/verdict inventory, prior certificate and creation state.
Collection rechecks genuine current original verdicts and keeps diagnostic-only
carrier observations separate from new mathematical reviews and certification.
It cannot substitute for a source repair, missing history or another gate defect.
If native collection cached its derivatives before that supplement, the guarded
`recover-operational-derived` command preserves the original collected, closed
and certification artifacts and records hash-bound immutable variants. Only the
normal mutable current-certificate pointer changes; certification starts from
the authenticated prior certificate and genuine native reviews, while unchanged
operational observations retain their original verdict coverage. Effective native
lookups validate that projection before using the corrected variants.
The owner-supervised wrapper forwards its reload version to the native stage
table and applies the owner hold before progress bookkeeping, so paused work
cannot cache derived collections before an authorized reconciliation.

An owner may admit an individually confirmed Step-4 reader concern about an
unchanged draft original-frontier item whose genuine original Luna verdict is
`keep:true`, before the first `impact-initial-1` owner pack freezes. The optional
`research/RUN-step5-reader-concern-admissions.json` is version 1, kind
`owner-confirmed-step4-reader-concerns`, authorized by `owner` with
`owner_identity: /root`, `native_coverage_adopted: false`, a dated record,
`original_count`, nonempty bounded `entries` and raw-SHA256 `bindings`.
Each entry names `id`, owning string `batch`, zero-based `concern_index`, the
exact original `concern` object, `before_guard_sha256`, and `owner_review`.
The review records `reviewed_by: root`, `confirmed_defect: true`, `reviewed_at`,
a concrete `reason`, and a bound focused `evidence_file`; exact proposed edits
use `proposed_edits: [{source_excerpt, proposed_replacement}]` with unique current
literal excerpts, or a bound `candidate_patch_file`. A single edit may place
`source_excerpt` and `proposed_replacement` directly on `owner_review`.
These are focused repair instructions, never preapplied source edits.

Bindings cover the immutable original frontier, baseline and verdict inventory;
the frozen initial pack and every genuine successful native per-unit initial
report/result (including unchanged mechanical zero-work reports); each current
owning batch manifest; the unchanged native Step-4 digest, successful Sol 6.1
medium reader result and exact attempt result and original structured output;
and focused root review evidence or candidate patches. Native preparation also
requires and binds the actual successful initial collection, once produced.
`node tools/step5-workflow.mjs check-reader-concerns --run RUN` validates the
admission read-only at the drained paused 5.1 boundary without claiming that
collection already exists. Preparation accepts only that boundary or drained 5.2
before owner dispatch; stale guards, missing individual confirmation, malformed or
foreign subjects, duplicate entries, or a late admission fail closed.

The first ordinary 5.2 pack unions these explicit concern subjects with real
consumer impacts and records their distinct origin. Mutable manifest preimages
are archived by the existing supporting-evidence mechanism. The admission grants
no worker execution, mathematical acceptance, judgment, or fatal-threshold credit,
and changes no frozen pack, native report or original verdict. Genuine 5.2
workers review and repair, 5.3 certifies, and 5.4 obtains current Sol judgments for
changed guards. Only actual Statement/Definition changes propagate consumers.
Concern-owning 5.2 lanes use persistent runtime homes under
`.autopilot/RUN/step5-reader-owner-sessions/uN`; necessary subsequent consumer
passes retain the supplier's owner and resume its authenticated successful native
session. Missing session continuity or conflicting reviewer ownership holds for
the root. Unrelated lanes retain their existing dispatch behavior, and all later
rounds, closure checks and complete gate batteries remain mandatory.

The additional
`proof-contract-coverage` mechanical check still requires a contract for each
actual proof-bearing carrier. No new substantive review gate is added. Step 6
performs mechanical contract closure and emits `step6-` owner-report artifacts;
its readiness and closeout commit remain evidence-bound. Publishing/pushing are
owner actions, separate from this build.

Fresh Step 6 uses metadata/render checks -> focused repair -> all final gates
(repeat after repairs) -> concise report -> scoped commit, for both mathematics
and physics. Every distinct mechanical condition and repair route remains;
identical checks run once. Readiness/report integrity hash only the frontier,
actual suppliers, owned evidence and workflow inputs. Git plumbing preserves
foreign working files by construction and verifies outside index flags/HEAD
metadata plus owned committed blobs inside the transaction. There is no
post-commit content gate battery. See [the implementation](tools/STEP6-REBUILD.md)
and [mechanical check map](tools/STEP6-MECHANICAL-CHECKS.md). New v3 stages require
an explicit guarded cutover for historical frozen runs; installation alone does
not migrate or resume them. Legacy closeout/recovery commands remain available
for their original historical receipts. Exact owner-authorized addition-only
published-ledger fragments are supported only by the v3 transaction: authority
and evidence are sealed before preparation, while separate current HEAD/index
foreign residuals and all working bytes are preserved at the actual ref boundary.
They grant record-level commit authority only, without mathematical acceptance
or ownership of the entire shared carrier. Conflicts fail closed.

    - title: Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6
      url: https://fncbook.com/integration/

## Example

Let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ be convex and Darboux integrable on $[a,b]$, with
$a<b$, and let $n\ge1$ be an integer. Then

$$Q_M(f;a,b,n)\le\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\le T_n(f),$$

where $Q_M$ is the composite midpoint value and $T_n(f)$ is the published
composite trapezoidal value of [[def-composite-trapezoidal-rule]] on the same
interval and uniform grid. Darboux integrability is the explicit premise that
makes the displayed Riemann integral defined. The proof uses convexity directly
for both inequalities and assumes no differentiability.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Reals $a<b$, an integer $n\ge1$, and a convex Darboux-integrable
$f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$.

[F1] [[def-convex-concave-and-midpoint-convex-functions]]: convexity means
$f(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)\le\lambda f(x)+(1-\lambda)f(y)$ for
$0\le\lambda\le1$.

[F2] [[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-darboux-equals-riemann]],
[[def-darboux-sums]], and [[def-partition-and-refinement]]: Darboux
integrability means the lower and upper integrals agree, and this integral
agrees with the tagged-Riemann definition.

[F3] [[lem-finite-sum-permutation-invariance]]: reordering a finite list of
terms by a permutation does not change its sum.

[F4] [[alg-composite-midpoint-rule]]: the composite midpoint value is the sum
of the panel midpoint values multiplied by the common width $h$.

[F5] [[def-composite-trapezoidal-rule]]: the composite value is $h$ times the
sum of endpoint values with half weights and interior node values with unit
weights.

[F6] [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]: pointwise order of integrable
functions on an increasing interval implies the same order for their
integrals.

[F7] [[thm-linearity-of-the-integral]]: sums and scalar multiples of
integrable functions are integrable, and their integrals are linear.

[F8] [[thm-additivity-over-subintervals]]: an integrable function remains
integrable on subintervals, and its integral adds over adjacent subintervals.

[F9] [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]]: affine functions and
polynomials are continuous.

[F10] [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]: every
continuous function on a closed interval (the case $q=1$) is Riemann
integrable.

[F11] [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]]: $(x^k)'=kx^{k-1}$ for each integer
$k\ge1$.

[F12] [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]: the sum, scalar-multiple, and product
rules give the corresponding derivatives.

[F13] [[thm-ftc-second-part]]: an integrable derivative has integral equal to
the endpoint increment of its antiderivative.

## Verification

1.1 Fix a panel $[u,v]=[x_j,x_{j+1}]$, write $h=v-u$ and $m=(u+v)/2$, and let $g(x):=f(u+v-x)$. The restriction of $f$ to this panel is integrable by [F8]. Reflect any partition of $[u,v]$ about $m$ and reverse the order of its nodes; this gives an involution on the set of partitions. Each reflected subinterval has the same length and the same range values of $g$ as the corresponding original subinterval has for $f$. Thus the lower and upper Darboux sums agree after reversing their finite lists of terms, by [F3]. Since the reflected partitions run through all partitions, [F2] shows that $g$ is integrable and $\int_u^v g=\int_u^v f$. [F2, F3, F8, construct]

1.2 For each panel put $u=x_j$, $v=x_{j+1}$ and $h=v-u$, and define the endpoint chord $L_j(x):=\frac{v-x}{h}f(u)+\frac{x-u}{h}f(v)$. For $x\in[u,v]$, the coefficients are in $[0,1]$ and sum to $1$, so [F1] gives $f(x)\le L_j(x)$. The functions are integrable by the given premise and by continuity of the affine chord [F9] with [F10]. Monotonicity [F6] gives $\int_u^v f\le\int_u^v L_j$. Set $$G_j(x):=f(u)(x-u)+\frac{f(v)-f(u)}{2h}(x-u)^2.$$ The power, product, sum, and scalar rules [F11, F12] give $G_j'=L_j$, so [F13] gives $\int_u^v L_j=G_j(v)-G_j(u)=\frac h2(f(u)+f(v))$. Summing over panels, additivity [F8] gives the integral over $[a,b]$, and each interior node is counted twice with half weight while each endpoint is counted once with half weight. By [F5] this sum is $T_n(f)$, so $\int_a^b f\le T_n(f)$. [given, F1, F5, F6, F8, F9, F10, F11, F12, F13, algebra]

2.1 For every $x\in[u,v]$, convexity [F1] at weight $1/2$ gives $2f(m)\le f(x)+g(x)$. The constant function is integrable by [F10], and $f+g$ is integrable by [F7] and step 1.1. Monotonicity [F6] and linearity [F7] therefore give $\int_u^v 2f(m)\,dx\le\int_u^v(f+g)\,dx=2\int_u^v f\,dx$. The function $G(x)=2f(m)x$ is an antiderivative of the constant integrand, by [F11] and [F12]. Hence [F13] gives $2h f(m)\le2\int_u^v f\,dx$, so $h f(m)\le\int_u^v f\,dx$. [given, F1, F6, F7, F10, F11, F12, F13, step 1.1]

3.1 Summing the panel inequalities from step 2.1 by [F8] and using the composite midpoint formula [F4] gives $Q_M(f;a,b,n)\le\int_a^b f$. Combining this with step 1.2 proves the bracketing. [step 2.1, step 1.2, F4, F8] ∎

## Example

On $[0,2]$, the function $f(x)=x^2$ has exact integral $8/3$. With $n=2$,
$h=1$, and the composite Simpson rule,

$$Q_S(f;0,2,2)=\frac13\bigl(f(0)+4f(1)+f(2)\bigr)=\frac83.$$

This is the quadratic case of exactness through degree three.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $f(x)=x^2$ on $[0,2]$ and the composite Simpson rule with $n=2$.

[F1] [[alg-composite-simpson-rule]]: for $n=2$, the returned value is
$\frac h3(f(x_0)+4f(x_1)+f(x_2))$.

[F2] [[thm-ftc-second-part]]: for an integrable derivative, the integral is
the increment of its antiderivative.

[F3] [[thm-composite-simpson-exact-through-degree-three]]: Simpson is exact
for every displayed polynomial of degree at most three.

[F4] [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]:
the power and scalar rules give $(x^3/3)'=x^2$.

[F5] [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]:
$x\mapsto x^2$ is Riemann integrable on $[0,2]$ because it is continuous.

## Verification

1.1 The function $x^2$ is continuous and integrable by [F5]. By [F4], $x^3/3$ is an antiderivative, so [F2] gives $\int_0^2x^2\,dx=8/3$. [given, F2, F4, F5]

2.1 Here $h=1$ and the nodes are $0,1,2$. By [F1], $Q_S=\frac13(0+4\cdot1+4)=8/3$. Thus the computed rule value equals the integral. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The equality also follows from the degree-at-most-three exactness theorem [F3], since $x^2$ has degree two. [F3, step 2.1] ∎

## Example

**Given:** The objective, start, initial matrices, direction, and step in the Example.

[F1] [[def-bfgs-curvature-pair-and-update-formulas]]: $s=\alpha p$, $y=g^+-g$, and $B^+=B-Bss^TB/(s^TBs)+yy^T/(s^Ty)$ when $s^Ty>0$.

[F2] [[alg-full-memory-bfgs-with-curvature-safeguards]]: an exact full-memory iteration uses $p=-Hg$ and accepts a positive strong Wolfe step before updating.

[F3] [[lem-bfgs-updates-preserve-secant-symmetry-and-spd]]: an SPD BFGS update with positive curvature satisfies $B^+s=y$ and remains SPD.

**Given:** The objective, start, initial matrices, direction, and step in the Example.

[F2] [[alg-full-memory-bfgs-with-curvature-safeguards]]: an exact full-memory iteration uses $p=-Hg$ and accepts a positive strong Wolfe step before updating.

[F3] [[lem-bfgs-updates-preserve-secant-symmetry-and-spd]]: an SPD BFGS update with positive curvature satisfies $B^+s=y$ and remains SPD.



1.1 The gradient is $\nabla f(x)=Ax$, so $g_0=(2,3)^T$ and the direction in [F2] is $p_0=-g_0=(-2,-3)^T$. Along this ray, $\phi'(t)=g_0^Tp_0+t\,p_0^TAp_0=-13+35t$, so the exact minimizer is $\alpha_0=13/35$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 At this step $\phi'(\alpha_0)=0$, which satisfies the strong curvature test for $c_2=2/5$. The quadratic identity $\phi(\alpha)=\phi(0)+\alpha\phi'(0)+\tfrac12\alpha^2p_0^TAp_0$ gives $\phi(\alpha_0)-\phi(0)=-169/70\le -(10^{-4})(169/35)=10^{-4}\alpha_0\phi'(0)$, so the strong Wolfe Armijo test also holds. [given, F2, algebra]

1.3 The step and gradient change are $s_0=\alpha_0p_0$ and $y_0=As_0=\alpha_0(-4,-9)^T$. Hence $s_0^Ty_0=35\alpha_0^2>0$ and $s_0^TB_0s_0=13\alpha_0^2>0$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Substitution in [F1] gives $$ B_1=I-\frac1{13}\begin{pmatrix}4&6\\6&9\end{pmatrix} +\frac1{35}\begin{pmatrix}16&36\\36&81\end{pmatrix} =\frac1{455}\begin{pmatrix}523&258\\258&1193\end{pmatrix}. $$ Multiplication yields $B_1s_0=\alpha_0(-4,-9)^T=y_0$. Consider the nonconvex function $f(x_1,x_2)=-\tfrac12x_1^2+\tfrac12x_2^2$ at $x=(1,0)^T$. The gradient is $g=(-1,0)^T$. The trial direction $p=(1,0)^T$ and trial step $\alpha=1$ give $s=(1,0)^T$ and $y=(-1,0)^T$. Use $B=H=I$ to compare the raw and Powell-damped updates.

[F2] [[lem-powell-damping-gives-positive-curvature]]: this damping rule gives $s^T\widetilde y=0.2c>0$ in the damped branch.

[F3] [[lem-bfgs-updates-preserve-secant-symmetry-and-spd]]: for SPD $B$ and positive damped curvature, the BFGS Hessian update remains SPD and satisfies $B^+s=\widetilde y$.

[F4] [[alg-full-memory-bfgs-with-curvature-safeguards]]: the normal search branch requires a strong Wolfe step and reports line-search failure if its finite search does not return one.

## Verification

[F2] [[lem-powell-damping-gives-positive-curvature]]: this damping rule gives $s^T\widetilde y=0.2c>0$ in the damped branch.

[F3] [[lem-bfgs-updates-preserve-secant-symmetry-and-spd]]: for SPD $B$ and positive damped curvature, the BFGS Hessian update remains SPD and satisfies $B^+s=\widetilde y$.

## Example

Compare the paired Hessian/inverse state used by the full-memory algorithm with the correction-pair storage in L-BFGS for $n=1000$ variables and memory length $m=10$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $n=1000$, $m=10$, a full $n\times n$ BFGS matrix, and the limited-memory state of [[alg-lbfgs-two-loop-with-curvature-filter]].

[F1] [[lem-lbfgs-two-loop-equals-stored-updates-and-cost]]: L-BFGS stores at most $m$ pairs of length-$n$ vectors and uses $O(mn)$ work for the two-loop recursion.

[F3] [[alg-full-memory-bfgs-with-curvature-safeguards]]: this fully explicit implementation maintains both consistent dense matrices $B_k$ and $H_k$.

[F2] [[alg-lbfgs-two-loop-with-curvature-filter]]: the working vectors have length $n$ and the stored memory is capped at $m$ pairs.

[F4] [[def-bfgs-curvature-pair-and-update-formulas]]: the direct update is $B^+=B-Bss^TB/(s^TBs)+yy^T/(s^Ty)$, and the inverse update is $H^+=(I-\rho sy^T)H(I-\rho ys^T)+\rho ss^T$, with $\rho=(s^Ty)^{-1}$.

## Verification

1.1 Each dense matrix contains $n^2=1000^2=1{,}000{,}000$ real entries. The paired state in [F3] therefore stores $2n^2=2{,}000{,}000$ matrix entries; a one-matrix implementation stores $n^2=1{,}000{,}000$. [given, F3, algebra]

1.2 The L-BFGS pair list contains at most $2mn=2\cdot10\cdot1000=20{,}000$ real coordinates, plus $O(n+m)$ temporary vectors and scalars. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 In exact inverse-matrix mode, computing $p=-Hg$ uses one dense matrix-vector product and costs $O(n^2)$ scalar operations. For the direct update, first compute $u:=Bs$ with one dense matrix-vector product; since $B$ is symmetric, $Bss^TB=uu^T$. Then form $B^+=B-uu^T/(s^Tu)+yy^T/(s^Ty)$ using two outer products and an entrywise matrix update, which costs $O(n^2)$. For the inverse update, first compute $v:=Hy$ with one dense matrix-vector product and expand [F4] using symmetry of $H$ to obtain $$H^+=H-\rho(sv^T+vs^T)+(\rho+\rho^2y^Tv)ss^T.$$ This uses a constant number of outer-product updates and also costs $O(n^2)$. Thus the dense direction and the paired BFGS updates use $O(n^2)$ work per iteration. By [F1], the two-loop recursion uses $O(mn)$ scalar work. Here $mn=10{,}000$ while $n^2=1{,}000{,}000$; the paired representation uses 100 times as many matrix entries as correction-pair coordinates, and a one-matrix representation uses 50 times as many. These are storage comparisons, not exact operation totals. [given, F1, F3, F4, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The example compares storage and update work only. It does not infer that L-BFGS has the same convergence rate as full BFGS; its convergence result requires separate curvature and scale bounds.

## Example

For an integer $m\ge3$, let $G$ be the star with center $0$ and leaves $1,\ldots,m$. Let $A=I+t\,\operatorname{Adj}(G)$, where $t=1/(2\sqrt m)$ and $\operatorname{Adj}(G)$ is the adjacency matrix. In leaf-first order, elimination adds no fill. In center-first order, symbolic elimination adds every edge between leaves, and the actual Cholesky Schur complement has all those entries nonzero.

## Facts & Assumptions


**Given:** An integer $m\ge3$, the star graph $G$, and the matrix $A$ specified above.

[F1] [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]]: At each step the graph deletes the pivot and adds every edge between distinct later neighbors.

## Verification


1.1 Write a vector as $x=(x_0,y_1,\ldots,y_m)$. The quadratic form is $x^TAx=x_0^2+\sum_i y_i^2+2t x_0\sum_i y_i$. Since $m\sum_i y_i^2-(\sum_i y_i)^2=\sum_{i<j}(y_i-y_j)^2\ge0$, we have $|\sum_i y_i|\le\sqrt m\,\|y\|_2$. Therefore [given, algebra]
$$2t|x_0|\left|\sum_i y_i\right|\le 2t\sqrt m\,|x_0|\|y\|_2\le t\sqrt m(x_0^2+\|y\|_2^2)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2.$$
It follows that $x^TAx\ge\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2>0$ for $x\ne0$, so $A$ is positive definite. [given, algebra]

1.2 In leaf-first order, each leaf has exactly one later neighbor, the center. By [F1] no pair of distinct remaining neighbors exists, so eliminating that leaf adds no edge. This holds for every leaf; eliminating the last center also adds no edge. [given, F1, algebra]

1.3 In center-first order, the center's later-neighbor set is all $m$ leaves. By [F1], the graph update inserts every pair of distinct leaves, so it has $\binom m2$ leaf-to-leaf fill edges not in the original star. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 The pivot at the center is $1$. Its Schur complement on the leaves is $I_m-t^2\mathbf1\mathbf1^T$, whose off-diagonal entries are $-t^2\ne0$. Thus the symbolic fill edges from step 1.3 are also numerical nonzeros for this matrix, while step 1.2 gives no fill in the other order. [step 1.2, step 1.3, given, algebra]

3.1 Steps 1.2 and 2.1 exhibit respectively $0$ and $\binom m2$ fill edges for two orderings of the same positive-definite sparse matrix. [step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

## Example

Take
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
This Hermitian matrix is nonsingular and indefinite. Every one-by-one diagonal pivot test fails, while the declared two-by-two pivot passes and gives an exact block $LDL^*$ factorization.

## Facts & Assumptions


**Given:** The matrix $A$ above, threshold $\theta\in(0,1]$, identity permutation, and the single declared pivot block of size two.

[F1] [[alg-symmetric-indefinite-block-ldl-star]]: A one-by-one pivot must be nonzero and pass the stated column threshold; a two-by-two pivot must be nonsingular and pass the componentwise inverse-block test.

## Verification


1.1 The determinant of $A$ is $-1$, so $A$ is nonsingular. Its eigenvectors $(1,1)^T$ and $(1,-1)^T$ have eigenvalues $1$ and $-1$, respectively; therefore $A$ is indefinite. [given, algebra]

1.2 Both diagonal candidates have pivot $0$, while the other entry in each column has modulus $1$. Since $\theta^{-1}|0|=0$, neither one-by-one test in [F1] passes. [given, F1, algebra]

1.3 For the declared block $D=A$, $\det D=-1\ne0$ and $D^{-1}=A$. There are no external indices, so $c_1=c_2=0$ and the two-by-two threshold left side is zero; the test in [F1] passes. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 The algorithm therefore returns $P=I$, $L=I$, and $D_{\rm blk}=A$. Direct multiplication gives $A=LD_{\rm blk}L^*$. Thus the block pivot succeeds where every one-by-one diagonal pivot fails. [step 1.3, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and let
$X,Y$ be Banach spaces over the same field $\mathbb F$. Let $U\subseteq X$ be
open and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable over
$\mathbb F$. Thus $F'(u)$ is bounded $\mathbb F$-linear for each $u\in U$ and
$$\lim_{\substack{h\to0,\ h\ne0\\u+h\in U}} \frac{\|F(u+h)-F(u)-F'(u)h\|}{\|h\|}=0.$$
In particular, in the complex case $F'(u)$ is complex-linear and the limit
ranges over complex increments. Let $K\subseteq U$ be convex and let
$x,z\in K$. If
$\|F'(u)-F'(v)\|\le L\|u-v\|$ for all $u,v\in K$, where $L\ge0$, then
$$\|F(x)-F(z)-F'(z)(x-z)\|\le\frac L2\|x-z\|^2.$$

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice, the Banach spaces and map in the Statement, the
convex set $K$, points $x,z\in K$, and the Lipschitz constant $L$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is the choice assumption used by the Banach-valued integral supplier.

[F1] [[lem-taylor-expansion-with-integral-remainder-for-banach-valued-curves]]: For a $C^1$ Banach-valued curve $\gamma$ on $[0,1]$, $\gamma(1)-\gamma(0)=\int_0^1\gamma'(t)\,dt$.

[F2] [[lem-linearity-of-the-bochner-integral]]: The Bochner integral is linear, and the integral of the constant function with value $v$ on $[0,1]$ is $v$.

[F3] [[lem-bochner-integral-norm-inequality]]: The norm of a Bochner integral is at most the integral of the norm of its integrand.

[F4] [[def-frechet-derivative-between-banach-spaces]]: In the real case the Fréchet derivative is bounded real-linear. In the complex case the same-field convention in the Statement makes it bounded complex-linear. In either case it is real-linear along real-parameter increments.

## Proof

**Given:** The assumptions and facts above. Put $h=x-z$ and
$\gamma(t)=F(z+th)$ for $0\le t\le1$.

1.1 Convexity gives $z+th\in K\subseteq U$ for $0\le t\le1$. If $h\ne0$ and $0<t<1$, put $u=z+th$. For real $s\to0$ with $t+s\in[0,1]$, Fréchet differentiability at $u$ gives $$\left\|\frac{F(u+sh)-F(u)}s-F'(u)h\right\| =\frac{\|F(u+sh)-F(u)-F'(u)(sh)\|}{|s|}\longrightarrow0,$$ because $F'(u)$ is linear over the common field and hence over real scalars. Thus $\gamma'(t)=F'(z+th)h$. If $h=0$, $\gamma$ is constant and the same formula holds. Differentiability at every point of $U$ also makes $F$ and hence $\gamma$ continuous on the segment, directly from the Fréchet remainder definition. In either case this derivative is continuous in $t$ and extends to the endpoints, since $F'$ is Lipschitz on $K$. The Banach-valued fundamental theorem [F1] therefore gives $F(x)-F(z)=\int_0^1F'(z+th)h\,dt$. The constant vector function $t\mapsto F'(z)h$ has integral $F'(z)h$ by [F2]. Subtracting that integral and using linearity gives $F(x)-F(z)-F'(z)h=\int_0^1(F'(z+th)-F'(z))h\,dt$. [A1, F1, F2, F4, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 For each $t\in[0,1]$, the Lipschitz hypothesis and bounded linearity give $\|(F'(z+th)-F'(z))h\|\le Lt\|h\|^2$. Therefore [F3] and scalar integration give $\|F(x)-F(z)-F'(z)h\|\le\int_0^1Lt\|h\|^2\,dt=(L/2)\|h\|^2$. [A1, step 1.1, F3, F4, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

[F5] [[def-bochner-integrable-function]]: A Bochner integral is defined as the norm limit of integrals of simple-function approximants for a Bochner-integrable function.

iterate $x_k$ minimizes $\|Ax-b\|_2$ over
$$x_0+\mathcal K_k(A^TA,A^Tr_0),$$
where $\mathcal K_k(M,v)=\operatorname{span}\{v,Mv,\ldots,M^{k-1}v\}$ is the
Krylov subspace of [[def-krylov-subspace-of-a-matrix-and-start-vector]].
The assertion is exact-arithmetic residual minimization; it is not a
convergence or noise-stability theorem.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The real matrix $A$, vectors $b,x_0$, and a nonbreakdown $k$-step
run of the LSQR algorithm.

[F1] [[alg-golub-kahan-lsqr-with-givens-and-status]]: The recurrences are
$\beta_{j+1}u_{j+1}=Av_j-\alpha_ju_j$ and
$\alpha_{j+1}v_{j+1}=A^Tu_{j+1}-\beta_{j+1}v_j$; the algorithm solves
$\min_z\|\beta_1e_1-B_jz\|_2$ and returns $x_j=x_0+V_jz$.

[F2] [[def-krylov-subspace-of-a-matrix-and-start-vector]]: For a square matrix
$M$ and vector $v$, $\mathcal K_k(M,v)=\operatorname{span}\{v,Mv,\ldots,M^{k-1}v\}$.

[F3] [[prop-krylov-subspace-is-the-polynomial-image-of-the-start-vector]]:
$\mathcal K_k(M,v)=\{p(M)v:p=0\text{ or }\deg p<k\}$.

[F4] [[thm-least-squares-solutions-and-normal-equation]]: A minimizer of a
finite-dimensional least-squares residual exists; a full-column-rank
coefficient matrix makes it unique.

[F5] [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]: $\langle u,v\rangle=u^Tv=\sum_i u_iv_i$ on each real coordinate space.

[F6] [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]: Matrix multiplication uses the finite row-coordinate sums.

[F7] [[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]]: $(A^T)_{ji}=a_{ij}$, so $\langle Av,u\rangle=\langle v,A^Tu\rangle$ by interchanging the two finite sums.

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses above, and write $V_j=[v_1,\ldots,v_j]$ and
$U_{j+1}=[u_1,\ldots,u_{j+1}]$.

1.1 The initial vector $u_1=r_0/\|r_0\|_2$ is unit. Suppose $u_1,\ldots,u_j$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_j$ are orthonormal and satisfy the earlier Golub–Kahan recurrences. For $i<j$, $\langle Av_j,u_i\rangle=\langle v_j,A^Tu_i\rangle=0$ by [F5]–[F7], because $A^Tu_i$ lies in $\operatorname{span}\{v_{i-1},v_i\}$; for $i=j$, $\langle Av_j,u_j\rangle=\alpha_j$ by the definition of $\alpha_j$. Therefore $Av_j-\alpha_ju_j$ is orthogonal to $u_1,\ldots,u_j$, and division by the nonzero $\beta_{j+1}$ gives a unit $u_{j+1}$ orthogonal to them. For $i<j$, $\langle A^Tu_{j+1},v_i\rangle=\langle u_{j+1},Av_i\rangle=0$ by [F5]–[F7], since $Av_i=\alpha_i u_i+\beta_{i+1}u_{i+1}$ lies in $\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\ldots,u_j\}$; for $i=j$ the inner product equals $\beta_{j+1}$. Thus $A^Tu_{j+1}-\beta_{j+1}v_j$ is orthogonal to $v_1,\ldots,v_j$, and division by the nonzero $\alpha_{j+1}$ gives a unit $v_{j+1}$ orthogonal to them. Induction proves both orthonormality relations through step $k$. [given, F1, F5, F6, F7, induction, algebra]

2.1 The column recurrences in [F1] assemble as $AV_k=U_{k+1}B_k$. Also $r_0=\beta_1u_1=\beta_1U_{k+1}e_1$. Hence for every $z\in\mathbb R^k$, $$b-A(x_0+V_kz)=r_0-AV_kz=U_{k+1}(\beta_1e_1-B_kz).$$ Orthonormality from [step 1.1] and the Euclidean norm definition [F5] imply $\|b-A(x_0+V_kz)\|_2=\|\beta_1e_1-B_kz\|_2$. [step 1.1, F1, F5, F6, algebra]

3.1 Each Givens rotation in [F1] is orthogonal because $(a/\rho)^2+(b/\rho)^2=1$ when $\rho=(a^2+b^2)^{1/2}>0$, so the rotations preserve the small least-squares residual norm. Since $B_k$ has nonzero diagonal $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k$, it has full column rank; [F4] therefore gives a unique minimizing vector $z_k$. The algorithm's $x_k=x_0+V_kz_k$ minimizes the true residual over $x_0+\operatorname{span}\{v_1,\ldots,v_k\}$ by [step 2.1]. [F1, F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The recurrence gives, for $j\ge1$, $$A^TAv_j=\alpha_j\beta_jv_{j-1}+(\alpha_j^2+\beta_{j+1}^2)v_j+\alpha_{j+1}\beta_{j+1}v_{j+1},$$ with the first term omitted at $j=1$. Every coefficient $\alpha_{j+1}\beta_{j+1}$ is nonzero in a nonbreakdown run, so induction shows $\operatorname{span}\{v_1,\ldots,v_k\}= \operatorname{span}\{v_1,A^TAv_1,\ldots,(A^TA)^{k-1}v_1\}$. Since $v_1=A^Tr_0/(\beta_1\alpha_1)$, [F2]–[F3] identify this span with $\mathcal K_k(A^TA,A^Tr_0)$. Substitution into [step 3.1] proves the Statement. [F1, F2, F3, F6, F7, step 3.1, induction, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:X\to Y$ and $\omega$ satisfy the
hypotheses of [[alg-landweber-iteration-with-discrepancy-stopping]] and put
$T=A^*A$. For each integer $k\ge0$, define
$g_0(t)=0$ and
$g_k(t)=\omega\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-\omega t)^j$ for $k\ge1$, with
$r_k(t)=(1-\omega t)^k$. For the associated infinite mathematical path,
$$x_k=g_k(T)A^*y_\delta,\qquad y_\delta-Ax_k=r_k(AA^*)y_\delta.$$
If $y_\delta=Ax^\dagger$, then
$$x^\dagger-x_k=r_k(T)x^\dagger.$$
Here $g_k(T)$ and $r_k(T)$ are the compact spectral multipliers defined in
[[def-compact-spectral-filter-and-qualification]]; $r_k(AA^*)$ is the
multiplier with scalar function $t\mapsto(1-\omega t)^k$ on the compact
self-adjoint operator $AA^*$, as supplied by
[[lem-compact-spectral-multiplier-is-well-defined]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice, compact nonzero $A:X\to Y$, $0<\omega<2/\|A\|^2$,
the algorithm's initial value $x_0=0$, and $T=A^*A$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is assumed by the Hilbert-adjoint and compact spectral multiplier suppliers used here.

[F1] [[alg-landweber-iteration-with-discrepancy-stopping]]: Its associated infinite path is defined for every $j\ge0$ by $x_{j+1}=x_j+\omega A^*(y_\delta-Ax_j)$; a finite run computes only a prefix.

[F2] [[lem-compact-gram-operator-is-positive-and-has-kernel]]: Both $A^*A$ and $AA^*$ are compact, positive, and self-adjoint, with $\ker(A^*A)=\ker A$.

[F3] [[lem-compact-spectral-multiplier-is-well-defined]]: Every bounded scalar function on the nonzero eigenspaces of a compact self-adjoint operator defines a bounded spectral multiplier.

[F4] [[def-compact-spectral-filter-and-qualification]]: For $T=A^*A$, compact spectral multipliers include the residual filter $r_k(t)=(1-\omega t)^k$.

[F5] [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]: $\langle Ax,y\rangle_Y=\langle x,A^*y\rangle_X$.

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses above and the exact recurrence [F1].

1.1 The adjoint identity [F5] gives $A^*A=T$. Thus [F1] rewrites each update before stopping as $x_{j+1}=(I-\omega T)x_j+\omega A^*y_\delta$. Starting from $x_0=0$, induction gives $x_k=\omega\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(I-\omega T)^jA^*y_\delta$: the sum is empty for $k=0$, and multiplying the $k$-term sum by $I-\omega T$ and adding $\omega A^*y_\delta$ produces the $(k+1)$-term sum. [A1, given, F1, F5, induction, algebra]

2.1 Put $\rho_k=y_\delta-Ax_k$. Substitution of [F1] gives $\rho_{k+1}=\rho_k-\omega AA^*\rho_k=(I-\omega AA^*)\rho_k$. Induction from $\rho_0=y_\delta$ yields $\rho_k=(I-\omega AA^*)^ky_\delta$. By [F2], $AA^*$ is compact positive self-adjoint, and [F3] therefore interprets this polynomial as the stated compact spectral multiplier. The scalar geometric identity $1-(1-\omega t)^k=\omega t\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-\omega t)^j$ also identifies the vector expression from step 1.1 with $g_k(T)A^*y_\delta$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, induction, algebra]

3.1 If $y_\delta=Ax^\dagger$, then [step 1.1] and $A^*y_\delta=Tx^\dagger$ give $x_k=\omega\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(I-\omega T)^jTx^\dagger=[I-(I-\omega T)^k]x^\dagger$ by the same polynomial identity. Since [F2] makes $T$ compact positive self-adjoint, [F4] interprets $r_k(T)$ as its residual multiplier; hence $x^\dagger-x_k=(I-\omega T)^kx^\dagger=r_k(T)x^\dagger$. [A1, F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces over the
same scalar field and let $U\subseteq X$ be open. Let $F:U\to Y$ be
continuously Fréchet differentiable over that field, with bounded
complex-linear derivatives in the complex case. Let $x^\dagger\in U$ satisfy
$F(x^\dagger)=y$, and suppose $x_k,x^\dagger$ lie in a convex subset of $U$
on which $F'$ is $L$-Lipschitz. Let $y_\delta$ satisfy
$\|y_\delta-y\|\le\delta$, put $e_k=x_k-x^\dagger$ and $A_k=F'(x_k)$,
and use the step of
[[alg-iteratively-regularized-gauss-newton-step]] with $\alpha_k>0$.
Define
$$R_k:=y-F(x_k)+A_ke_k.$$
Then
$$e_{k+1}=\alpha_k(A_k^*A_k+\alpha_kI)^{-1}e_k +(A_k^*A_k+\alpha_kI)^{-1}A_k^*(y_\delta-y+R_k),$$
and
$$\|e_{k+1}\|\le\|e_k\|+ \frac{\delta+(L/2)\|e_k\|^2}{2\sqrt{\alpha_k}}.$$
If in addition the tangential-cone condition
$$\|F(x)-F(z)-F'(z)(x-z)\|\le\eta\|F(x)-F(z)\|$$
holds for all $x,z$ in that subset, then also
$\|R_k\|\le\eta(\|F(x_k)-y_\delta\|+\delta)$, which may replace
$(L/2)\|e_k\|^2$ in the recurrence bound. This lemma alone does not assert
contraction or discrepancy-stopped convergence.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Hilbert-space data and iterates above, $\alpha_k>0$, the
Lipschitz derivative bound, and, for the final bound, the stated tangential
cone condition.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is assumed by the Hilbert adjoint and shifted-normal-operator suppliers.

[F1] [[alg-iteratively-regularized-gauss-newton-step]]: $e_{k+1}=e_k+s_k$ and $(A_k^*A_k+\alpha_kI)s_k=A_k^*(y_\delta-F(x_k))$.

[F2] [[lem-hilbert-tikhonov-normal-operator-invertible]]: $B_k=A_k^*A_k+\alpha_kI$ is invertible with $\|B_k^{-1}\|\le1/\alpha_k$.

[F3] [[lem-hilbert-tikhonov-noise-amplification-bound]]: $\|B_k^{-1}A_k^*v\|\le\|v\|/(2\sqrt{\alpha_k})$ for bounded $A_k$.

[F4] [[lem-local-lipschitz-derivative-quadratic-remainder]]: $\|F(x)-F(z)-F'(z)(x-z)\|\le(L/2)\|x-z\|^2$ on the convex subset.

## Proof

**Given:** The assumptions and facts above. Put
$B_k=A_k^*A_k+\alpha_kI$.

1.1 From [F1], $e_{k+1}=e_k+B_k^{-1}A_k^*(y_\delta-F(x_k))$. Multiplying by $B_k$ and using $B_ke_k=A_k^*A_ke_k+\alpha_ke_k$ gives $$B_ke_{k+1}=\alpha_ke_k+A_k^*(A_ke_k+y_\delta-F(x_k)).$$ Since $A_ke_k+y-F(x_k)=R_k$, the term in parentheses is $y_\delta-y+R_k$. Applying [F2] to invert $B_k$ proves the stated identity. [A1, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 By [F2], $\|\alpha_kB_k^{-1}e_k\|\le\|e_k\|$. By [F3], $\|B_k^{-1}A_k^*(y_\delta-y+R_k)\| \le(\delta+\|R_k\|)/(2\sqrt{\alpha_k})$. The triangle inequality and [F4] give the quadratic-error recurrence. [A1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For the tangential-cone bound, substitute $x=x^\dagger$ and $z=x_k$. Its left side is $\|y-F(x_k)+A_k(x_k-x^\dagger)\|=\|R_k\|$, so $\|R_k\|\le\eta\|y-F(x_k)\|\le\eta(\|y-y_\delta\|+\|y_\delta-F(x_k)\|) \le\eta(\delta+\|y_\delta-F(x_k)\|)$. Inserting this estimate into the bound from [step 2.1] proves the optional residual form. [A1, given, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:X\to Y$ be a nonzero compact operator between
real or complex Hilbert spaces, set $T=A^*A$, choose
$0<\omega<2/\|A\|^2$, and let $y=Ax^\dagger$ with
$x^\dagger\in(\ker A)^\perp$. Let $x_k$ be the exact-data Landweber iterates
in the infinite recurrence-defined path of
[[alg-landweber-iteration-with-discrepancy-stopping]] for datum $y$; this path
depends on $A,\omega,y$ and not on a finite cap or stopping test. Put
$r_k(t)=(1-\omega t)^k$. Then $\|x_k-x^\dagger\|$ is nonincreasing and
$x_k\to x^\dagger$ in norm. For every $s>0$, if $x^\dagger=T^s w$ with
$w\in X$, then for $k\ge1$,
$$\|x_k-x^\dagger\|\le C_{s,A,\omega}\|w\|k^{-s}.$$
The scalar filter also satisfies
$$\sup_{t\in\Sigma}t^s|r_k(t)|\le C_{s,A,\omega}k^{-s},$$
where $\Sigma$ is the set of nonzero eigenvalues of $T$.
For noisy data $y_\delta$ with $\|y_\delta-y\|\le\delta$, let
$x_k^\delta$ be the infinite recurrence-defined path for datum $y_\delta$.
It satisfies
$$\|x_k^\delta-x_k\|\le\sqrt{2\omega k}\,\delta.$$
Consequently, under the source condition $x^\dagger=T^\nu w$,
$0<\nu\le1$, the total error obeys
$$\|x_k^\delta-x^\dagger\|\le C_{\nu,A,\omega}\|w\|k^{-\nu} +\sqrt{2\omega k}\,\delta.$$

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice; the stated $A,\omega,y,x^\dagger$; and
$T=A^*A$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is assumed by the Hilbert-adjoint and compact spectral theorem suppliers used in this proof.

[F1] [[lem-landweber-filter-and-residual-identities]]: For the infinite mathematical path, $x_k=g_k(T)A^*y_\delta$ and, for exact data, $x^\dagger-x_k=r_k(T)x^\dagger$.

[F2] [[def-compact-spectral-filter-and-qualification]]: $T^\nu$ and the filters are defined by their scalar values on the nonzero eigenvalues of the compact positive operator $T$.

[F3] [[lem-compact-gram-operator-is-positive-and-has-kernel]]: $T$ is compact positive self-adjoint and $\ker T=\ker A$.

[F4] [[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]]: $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$ and $\|Q\|^2=\|QQ^*\|$ for bounded Hilbert-space operators.

[F5] [[def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]: $x^\dagger\in(\ker A)^\perp$ means it has no component in the zero eigenspace of $T$.

[F6] [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-compact-self-adjoint-operators]]: The nonzero eigenspaces of compact self-adjoint $T$ are mutually orthogonal, at most countably many, and together with $\ker T$ have dense span in $X$.

[F7] [[lem-compact-spectral-multiplier-is-well-defined]]: A bounded scalar multiplier on these eigenspaces defines an operator whose norm is at most the supremum of the multiplier's absolute value.

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses and facts above. Write $M=\|A\|^2$.

1.1 For every nonzero eigenvalue $t$ of $T$, [F3]–[F4] give $0<t\le M$, so $0<\omega t<2$ and $|1-\omega t|<1$. Therefore $|r_k(t)|$ decreases with $k$ and tends to $0$. Since $x^\dagger\perp\ker T$ by [F3] and [F5], [F6] expands it using only positive-eigenvalue components. By [F1], each component of $x_k-x^\dagger$ is multiplied by $-r_k(t)$; its magnitude decreases to zero and is bounded by the corresponding component of $x^\dagger$. Given $\epsilon>0$, choose a finite set of eigenvalues whose omitted squared components of $x^\dagger$ sum to less than $\epsilon$; on the chosen finite set every component tends to zero. The squared error sum therefore tends to at most $\epsilon$, and arbitrariness of $\epsilon$ proves norm convergence. The componentwise decrease also proves monotonicity of the norm. [A1, F1, F3, F4, F5, F6, given, choose]

1.2 Choose an integer $m>s$. For $v\ge0$ and an integer $n\ge0$,
$(1+v)^n\ge1+nv$: induction proves this, since multiplying the bound at
$n$ by $1+v$ gives $1+(n+1)v+nv^2\ge1+(n+1)v$. For $k\ge2m$, let
$n=\lfloor k/m\rfloor$, so $mn\le k$ and $n\ge k/(2m)$.
If $0<t\le\min\{M,\omega^{-1}\}$, put $u=\omega t\in(0,1]$. At $u=1$
the filter is zero. If $0<u\le1/k$, then $u^s(1-u)^k\le k^{-s}$. If
$k\ge2m$ and $1/k<u<1$, the identity $(1-u)(1+u)=1-u^2\le1$ gives
$(1-u)^{-k}\ge(1+u)^k\ge(1+u)^{mn}=((1+u)^n)^m\ge(nu)^m$.
Consequently
$$u^s(1-u)^k\le n^{-m}u^{s-m}\le n^{-m}k^{m-s} \le(2m)^m k^{-s}.$$
For $k<2m$ the same product is at most $1\le(2m)^s k^{-s}$. Thus on this
range $t^s|r_k(t)|=\omega^{-s}u^s(1-u)^k\le C_{s,\omega}k^{-s}$.
If $\omega^{-1}<t\le M$, a range that exists only when $\omega M>1$, then
$|1-\omega t|=\omega t-1\le\omega M-1=:q\in(0,1)$. Put
$a=q^{-1}-1>0$. For $k\ge2m$ and the same $n$,
$$q^{-k}=(1+a)^k\ge(1+a)^{mn}=((1+a)^n)^m\ge(na)^m,$$
so $k^s q^k\le(2m)^m a^{-m}k^{s-m}\le(2m)^m a^{-m}$. For $k<2m$,
$k^s q^k\le(2m)^s$. Hence $\sup_{k\ge1}k^s q^k<\infty$ and
$t^s|r_k(t)|\le M^s q^k\le C_{s,M,\omega}k^{-s}$. Combining the two
ranges proves $\sup_{t\in\sigma(T)\setminus\{0\}}t^s|r_k(t)|\le
C_{s,A,\omega}k^{-s}$. [A1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

1.3 For $k\ge1$, the scalar geometric identity gives $g_k(t)=[1-(1-\omega t)^k]/t$ for $t>0$. Since $|1-\omega t|\le1$, both the bound by $2$ and the finite-sum bound by $k\omega t$ hold for its numerator. Hence $$\sqrt t\,|g_k(t)|\le\min\{2/\sqrt t,\omega k\sqrt t\}\le\sqrt{2\omega k}.$$ The last inequality follows by splitting at $t=2/(\omega k)$. For $Q_k=g_k(T)A^*$, adjoint multiplication gives $Q_kQ_k^*=g_k(T)Tg_k(T)^*$, the compact spectral multiplier with scalar values $t|g_k(t)|^2$ and value zero on $\ker T$. [F7] bounds its norm by the supremum of these values; [F4] and $\|Q_k\|^2=\|Q_kQ_k^*\|$ then give $\|Q_k\|\le\sqrt{2\omega k}$. Applying [F1] to $y_\delta-y$ gives $\|x_k^\delta-x_k\|=\|Q_k(y_\delta-y)\|\le\sqrt{2\omega k}\,\delta$. [A1, F1, F4, F7, given, algebra]

2.1 Under $x^\dagger=T^sw$, [F1] gives $x_k-x^\dagger=-r_k(T)T^sw$. On every eigenspace the product multiplier is $t^sr_k(t)$, bounded by [step 1.2]; [F7] therefore yields $\|x_k-x^\dagger\|\le\sup_{t>0}t^s|r_k(t)|\,\|w\|$. Substituting the bound in [step 1.2] proves the source-bias estimate. [A1, F1, F2, F7, step 1.2, algebra]

## Statement

$x^\dagger=T^\nu w$ with $0<\nu\le1$ and $R=\|w\|\ge0$. Fix $\tau>1$ and

first index on the associated infinite mathematical path satisfying
$\|Ax_{k_\delta}^\delta-y_\delta\|\le\tau\delta$, where $x_k^\delta$ is
the corresponding noisy-data path.
If a finite budget is used, assume it is at least the upper bound $K_\delta$
constructed in the proof when $R>0$. If $R=0$, the initial iterate is the
first crossing and any finite budget suffices. For all sufficiently small
$\delta$,
$$\|x_{k_\delta}^\delta-x^\dagger\| \le C_{\nu,A,\omega,\tau}R^{1/(2\nu+1)}\delta^{2\nu/(2\nu+1)}.$$
The conclusion is conditional on an actual discrepancy crossing; a budget
exhaustion status is inconclusive.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The stated compact operator, Landweber parameter, source condition,
noise bound, $\tau>1$, and the first discrepancy index.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: Countable Choice is assumed by the compact spectral and Hilbert-adjoint suppliers used in the proof.

[F1] [[thm-landweber-source-and-noise-error-bounds]]: For every $s>0$, $\sup_{t\in\Sigma}t^s|r_k(t)|\le C_{s,A,\omega}k^{-s}$; the noise amplification is at most $\sqrt{2\omega k}\delta$.

[F2] [[lem-landweber-filter-and-residual-identities]]: $y_\delta-Ax_k^\delta=r_k(AA^*)y_\delta$ and $x^\dagger-x_k=r_k(T)x^\dagger$.

[F3] [[def-compact-spectral-filter-and-qualification]]: $T^\nu$ and $r_k(T)$ act by their scalar multipliers on each nonzero eigenspace.

[F4] [[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]]: $\|Av\|^2=\langle A^*Av,v\rangle$, $\|A^*\|=\|A\|$, and $\|Q\|^2=\|QQ^*\|$ for bounded Hilbert-space operators.

[F5] [[lem-compact-spectral-multiplier-is-well-defined]]: A compact spectral multiplier has operator norm at most the supremum of the absolute values of its scalar multipliers.

[F6] [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-compact-self-adjoint-operators]]: The eigenspaces of compact self-adjoint $T$ are mutually orthogonal and, together with $\ker T$, have dense span.

[F7] [[lem-compact-gram-operator-is-positive-and-has-kernel]]: Both $A^*A$ and $AA^*$ are compact, positive, and self-adjoint; $\ker(A^*A)=\ker A$.

**Given:** The hypotheses above, with $R\ge0$.

If $R=0$, then $w=0$, so $x^\dagger=0$ and $y=Ax^\dagger=0$. The initial
iterate $x_0^\delta=0$ has residual $\|Ax_0^\delta-y_\delta\|=\|y_\delta\|

zero, which is the stated estimate with $R=0$ since $0^a=0$ for every $a>0$.

1.1 Put $p=\nu+\tfrac12$. By [F2], $x_k-x^\dagger=-r_k(T)T^\nu w$. The compact spectral expansion [F6], the power convention [F3], and $\|Az\|^2=\langle A^*Az,z\rangle$ from [F4] give $\|Ax_k-y\|=\|T^p r_k(T)w\|$. The scalar filter bound [F1] therefore gives $\|Ax_k-y\|\le C_{p,A,\omega}Rk^{-p}$. Choose $$K_\delta=\max\!\left\{1,\left\lceil\left(\frac{C_{p,A,\omega}R}{(\tau-1)\delta}\right)^{1/p}\right\rceil\right\}.$$ Then $\|Ax_{K_\delta}-y\|\le(\tau-1)\delta$. Every eigenvalue $t$ of $AA^*$ therefore satisfies $0\le t\le\|A\|^2$, so $|1-\omega t|\le1$ by the step-size hypothesis. [F5] bounds the noise residual by $\delta$. Hence $\|Ax_{K_\delta}^\delta-y_\delta\|\le\tau\delta$, so the first crossing exists and $k_\delta\le K_\delta$ (provided the finite budget reaches $K_\delta$). [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 At the crossing, [F2] and the same multiplier estimate [F5] give $\|Ax_{k_\delta}-y\|\le\|Ax_{k_\delta}^\delta-y_\delta\|+\delta\le(\tau+1)\delta$. [A1, F2, F5, given, algebra]

2.1 Let $v=r_{k_\delta}(T)w$ and $\theta=2\nu/(2\nu+1)$. For a finite set $E\subseteq\Sigma$, put $a_t=t^{2\nu+1}\|P_tv\|^2$ and $b_t=\|P_tv\|^2$. Then $t^{2\nu}\|P_tv\|^2=a_t^\theta b_t^{1-\theta}$. 3.1 From [F1], $\|x_{k_\delta}^\delta-x_{k_\delta}\|\le\sqrt{2\omega K_\delta}\delta$. Put $B=C_{p,A,\omega}R/(\tau-1)$, choosing $C_{p,A,\omega}>0$. ## Statement refuted

There is a constant independent of the matrix such that continuing the LSQR
projected solves to zero residual always gives an estimate within that
constant times the data-noise level of the exact solution.

## Concrete instance

For each integer $N\ge2$, let
$A_N=\operatorname{diag}(1,N^{-2})$, exact solution $x^\dagger=0$, exact
datum $y=0$, and noisy datum $y^\delta=(0,N^{-1})^T$. The noise level is
$\delta_N=N^{-1}\to0$. The un-stopped projected LSQR solve takes one
Golub–Kahan step and returns $x_1^\delta=(0,N)^T$ with zero residual. Thus
the error is $N$, which is not bounded by a fixed multiple of $\delta_N$.
With the assigned discrepancy-stopped procedure and zero initial guess, the
initial residual already satisfies $\|r_0\|=\delta_N\le\tau\delta_N$;
the procedure returns at index zero. The example concerns continuing to a
full solve and shows why early stopping matters.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The diagonal matrix, exact and noisy data, and zero initial guess.

[F1] [[alg-golub-kahan-lsqr-with-givens-and-status]]: The un-stopped version
uses the stated LSQR initialization and first projected solve; the assigned
procedure itself may return earlier at its discrepancy check.

[F2] [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]: Matrix-vector multiplication is the coordinate sum of each row against the vector.

[F3] [[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]]: $(A^T)_{ji}=a_{ij}$.

[F4] [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]: $\|u\|_2=(u^Tu)^{1/2}$ on real coordinate vectors.

[F5] [[def-natural-numbers]]: The iteration dimension parameter $N$ is a natural number with $N\ge2$.

[F6] [[def-matrix-space]]: $A_N$ is a real $2\times2$ matrix and acts on real coordinate vectors by matrix multiplication.

## Refutation

1.1 For $A_N$ and $y^\delta$, $r_0=(0,N^{-1})^T$, so $\beta_1=N^{-1}$, $u_1=(0,1)^T$, $\alpha_1=N^{-2}$, and $v_1=(0,1)^T$. The first bidiagonalization residual is $A_Nv_1-\alpha_1u_1=0$, so $\beta_2=0$ and the one-dimensional projected least-squares problem is exact. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, algebra]

2.1 Its scalar matrix is $B_1=(N^{-2})$ and right-hand side is $\beta_1e_1=N^{-1}e_1$, so the unique minimizer is $z_1=N$. Consequently $x_1^\delta=x_0+Nv_1=(0,N)^T$, $A_Nx_1^\delta=y^\delta$, and $\|x_1^\delta-x^\dagger\|_2=N$. The noise is $\|y^\delta-y\|_2=N^{-1}$, so the error-to-noise ratio is $N^2\to\infty$. This refutes the proposed uniform bound and shows that the projected solve can fit a small noise component in a weak singular direction. The terminal $\beta_2=0$ is the algorithm's breakdown branch after the projected iterate has been formed, so this calculation does not invoke a nonbreakdown theorem. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
